philosophy.title: Six principles, written into the product.
philosophy.desc: GEO is not a trick played on the engines. It is the discipline of putting true, findable facts where AI looks — and measuring honestly whether AI picks them up. Every principle below is a feature in the workspace, not a line on a slide.

cards.title: Facts live on your site, not in our app
cards.desc: AI can only repeat what is public. So the platform never becomes the place where truth is kept: it reads your own pages, shows where AI contradicts them or finds nothing, and sends you back to fix the source. No hidden database of “verified facts”.

cards.title: Define the standard; don't compete on scale
cards.desc: Presence, share of voice, prominence, sentiment, citation — every rate published with its numerator and denominator, sample sizes and confidence labels, in a public Measurement Standard (v1.1) anyone can check. Plans differ in scope, never in method.

cards.title: Honest measurement
cards.desc: A frozen prompt panel per market, the real Google AI Overview page, judged answers you can open and re-check. An effect is reported only when the targeted prompts beat the control prompts by more than 10 points. We never promise rankings or sales.

cards.title: Feedback kept in the system becomes an asset
cards.desc: Every competitor you re-tag, every prompt you reword, every action you log is recorded with its reason and re-applied on every re-run. Your team's judgement compounds inside the platform instead of evaporating in chat threads.

cards.title: One person + AI helpers closes a loop
cards.desc: The workspace is built for a minimal unit: one owner and scoped agents that sense, judge, act, measure and record on their own. Your team specifies and gives feedback; the platform side builds the agents. No engineering hires on your side.

cards.title: Be the source
cards.desc: AI trusts a short list of domains in each market. We rank them across every scan, fetch and profile the pages they cite, publish the Vietnam list monthly, and verify what you put live — so your pages and the media AI already cites carry your facts.

tech.title:

The domains AI cites in your market, ranked across scans; the cited pages fetched and profiled (structure, freshness, schema) so content is written to a measured bar. Your own pages join the corpus: site coverage and contradictions in every report.

Publish-ready pages and FAQ, paste-in JSON-LD, placement kits for the sources AI trusts (competitors excluded), encyclopedia drafts with a compliant path. Numbers without a source become placeholders, never inventions.
Log what went live; we fetch it, hash it and attribute what moved by question and engine. Stage-aware weekly digests, monthly reports, alerts on drops — and your edits survive every re-run.

market.insight_body: English-language AI cognition for global brands is already a red ocean. In Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Malay and Filipino, the AI knowledge layer is still largely vacant — first movers write the default answer. And in the United States, buyers ask AI with a state attached ("best injury lawyer in Texas"), and the correct, compliant answer differs at the state line — a national score hides where you actually win or lose.

steps.title: Profile, panel, first scan

steps.desc: Scheduled scans on the frozen panel keep scores comparable. Effect = change on the prompts you targeted minus change on the control prompts; only changes above 10 points count. Digest to the inbox, alerts on drops, credits for “run it now”.

faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.desc: The answers we give most often — written so AI engines can quote them cleanly too.

items.a: GEO is the practice of optimizing how a brand is represented inside generative AI engines such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overview. Where SEO targets a ranked list of links, GEO targets the answer itself — whether your brand is mentioned, how prominently, how accurately, and which sources the engine cites.

items.q: How is GEO different from SEO?
items.a: SEO optimizes for ranking in a list of blue links; GEO optimizes for inclusion, accuracy and prominence inside a generated answer. The levers differ: structured data, authoritative third-party citations, canonical answers to buyer questions, and content written to be cited — not backlinks and keyword density.

items.q: What does MemeCMO measure, and how?
items.a: Five standard metrics per engine, each with its numerator and denominator: presence (answers mentioning you ÷ all answers), share of voice (your mentions ÷ all tracked-brand mentions, sums to 100%), prominence, sentiment when present, and citation (answers citing your own domain). Plus top-of-mind rate and a high-intent gap list. Everything is measured on a frozen prompt panel per market and defined in the public AI Visibility Measurement Standard v1.1.

items.q: How do you stop the AI from inventing facts?
items.a: Content agents may only use figures from your brand profile and the documents you upload; any number without a source becomes a placeholder for you to fill. Competitor and vendor domains are excluded from placement targets, calques are rewritten into market phrasing, unsourced claims are flagged, and nothing is published by us — you publish, then log the action and we verify it.

A public document (v1.1, September 2026) that defines every metric, the sampling design, confidence labels, citation coverage (4/5 engines), comparison against the client's own public pages, verification of logged actions and the rule for publishing source lists. Every number the platform shows can be traced to it. Read the standard →

items.q: Which AI engines and markets are covered?
items.a: ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude and the real Google AI Overview page, location-targeted. Markets: Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines in their local languages, and the United States state by state (Tier-1: California, Texas, Florida, New York), with state-law frames for regulated verticals.

Three plans per brand × market: Starter US$99, Growth US$199 and Scale US$1,999+ per month. The plan sets the scheduled scan cadence, prompt panel size, engines, projects, report frequency and included credits; scheduled scans and reports are included. Credits pay only for runs you trigger yourself. Seats are unlimited; agency partners get a workspace per client and wholesale pricing. Plans, credits and service items →

items.q: Who owns the data — and the feedback?
items.a: Your brand facts, marks and documents stay yours; the platform, prompt method and scoring rules are ours. Every correction your team makes — a re-tagged competitor, a reworded prompt, a logged action — is recorded with its reason and reused, so the feedback becomes your project's asset. You can export your full history up to 12 months after termination, and any figure we publish comes from at least 5 brands, de-identified.

Brands entering Southeast Asia — especially Chinese companies going global — regional brands defending their home market, US brands in regulated verticals where answers differ by state, and the agencies and media groups that serve them as channel partners.

items.q: How is MemeCMO different from Semrush, Profound or other GEO tools?
items.a: Most GEO tools stop at monitoring: they show you a dashboard and leave the work to you. MemeCMO's ten agents also produce the deliverables — standard answers, JSON-LD schema, gap content, placements, encyclopedia entries — grounded only in your public facts, and then verify what you publish and attribute what moved. Two more differences: a public measurement standard behind every number, and market depth others lack — Southeast Asian languages and US state-by-state measurement. Full comparison with sources →
